story.headline: Design the first-use flow your developer will build.
story.body: Review one existing onboarding or first-use flow, up to five screens. Get annotated Figma screens, a clickable prototype, one handoff call and one revision.
story.reason: Leads with the founder’s design task and connects the design work to implementation by their developer.

resonance.headline: For SaaS founders revisiting their product’s first-use flow.
resonance.body: For solo founders and small founder-led teams with an existing SaaS product: one flow, up to five screens, with annotated Figma screens, a clickable prototype, one handoff call and one revision.
resonance.reason: Makes the audience and existing-product situation explicit so founders can judge whether the service fits their current work.

offer.headline: One flow, up to five screens, with a clickable prototype.
offer.body: Receive annotated Figma screens, one handoff call and one revision for an existing onboarding or first-use flow. Bring a product link or walkthrough recording and your chosen first-use task.
offer.reason: Puts the bounded scope and tangible deliverables first, then states what the founder brings to the work.

tradeoff: Story connects the founder’s next design task to their developer’s implementation. Resonance identifies the audience more directly, while offer gives the five-screen boundary more prominence.
limitations: Editorial disclosure outside hero copy: Mina Studio and its persona are fictional demo material. The AI-generated portrait represents that fictional persona. Keep the separate visible disclosure in implementation.
The portrait is not a real customer, testimonial, founder of Landing Page Lab, or evidence of results. No real clients, results, availability, booking, reputation, or person are evidenced.
Mina Studio is an independent product-design service for solo SaaS founders and small founder-led software teams with an existing product.
The scope is one existing onboarding or first-use flow, up to five screens, with annotated Figma screens, a clickable prototype, one handoff call and one revision.
The founder supplies a product link or walkthrough recording, their chosen first-use task, and existing design files where available. Their developer implements the design.
Implementation, user interviews, brand identity, ongoing support, and a full product redesign are outside scope. Price, timeline, client results and guarantees are unknown.
The CTA links to a local illustrative sample project, not a contact or booking action.
Across the comparison, retain one human portrait and the same typography, background and layout.
